step1_figure.circuit_type: DC Generation Circuit (Peak/Valley Detector and Average Reference Generator) with Low Input Resistance Channel Buffer
step1_figure.description: Figure 18.28 shows the complete DC generation circuit consisting of a peak detector, valley detector, resistive averaging network, and output slicing buffer. Figure 18.30 provides the front-end transmission channel model and input resistor divider (R3=1k, C4=10pF, R4=1k to VDD, R5=1k to GND) that reduces the effective channel time constant.

effective_channel_time_constant.description: Effective RC time constant of the bandlimited transmission channel loaded by the low-input-resistance termination network

equation.explanation: Connecting two 1k termination resistors (R4 to VDD, R5 to GND) in parallel with the 1k channel resistor lowers the equivalent Thevenin resistance seen by the 10pF channel capacitor from 1k to 333.3 ohms, reducing the time constant.
equation.assumptions: Buffer inputs present purely capacitive high input impedance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined purely by the channel and termination passive network values (three 1k resistors and 10pF capacitor).

input_attenuation_factor.description: DC voltage division ratio from channel input (Vin) to buffer input node (In)

equation.explanation: The two 1k resistors to VDD and GND form a Thevenin equivalent of 500 ohms, creating a 1:3 voltage divider with the 1k series resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: A_v = 500 / 1500 = 0.333 (-9.54 dB). For a 0 to 1.8V input swing, Delta_Vin = 1.8V / 3 = 0.60V.

input_node_dc_voltage_range.description: Minimum and maximum voltage levels at node In when Vin swings rail-to-rail (0 to 1.8V)

equation.formula: V_{in,low} = VDD \cdot \frac{R_3 \parallel R_5}{R_4 + R_3 \parallel R_5} = \frac{VDD}{3}; \; V_{in,high} = VDD \cdot \frac{R_5}{R_5 + R_3 \parallel R_4} = \frac{2\cdot VDD}{3}
equation.explanation: When Vin=0V, R3 and R5 are in parallel to GND (500 ohm) against R4 to VDD (1k), giving 1/3 VDD. When Vin=VDD, R3 and R4 are in parallel to VDD (500 ohm) against R5 to GND (1k), giving 2/3 VDD.
equation.assumptions: Full rail input pulses (0 to 1.8V) at low enough frequency to allow steady-state charging.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Superposition of VDD through R4 and Vin through R3 onto node In.

dc_reference_average_voltage.description: DC slicing threshold voltage generated at node Avg by averaging the peak and valley voltages

equation.explanation: The two equal 100k resistors average the peak detector output (Vmax) and the valley detector output (Vmin) to produce the center slicing reference.
equation.assumptions: R1 = R2 = 100k, input data has approximately 50% duty cycle.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetrical swing around VDD/2 yields an average exactly at 0.90 V.

averaging_filter_time_constant.description: RC time constant of the running average network filtering node Avg

equation.explanation: The Thevenin resistance seen by the 1pF filter capacitor C3 looking into the midpoint between R1 and R2 is R1 || R2.
equation.assumptions: Peak and valley capacitors C1 and C2 act as low-impedance sources for the filter.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_th = 100k || 100k = 50 kOhm; C3 = 1 pF; tau_avg = 50e3 * 1e-12 = 50 ns. Settling to 90% takes ~2.3 * tau_avg = 115 ns; steady-state by ~150 to 200 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 50 kOhm parallel resistance with 1 pF capacitor.

slicing_buffer_output_swing.description: Output high and low voltage levels of the final data slicing buffer (X_U3)

equation.explanation: The output stage of the buffer SUB_1 is a CMOS inverter (xm5 and xm7) driving the output rail-to-rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_{OH} = 1.8 V, V_{OL} = 0.0 V, full swing = 1.8 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS push-pull inverter output pulls completely to the supply rails when unloaded.

slicing_buffer_propagation_delay.description: Propagation delay from input signal crossing Vavg to output transition crossing 50% VDD

equation.explanation: Delay through the complementary self-biased differential amplifier and output inverter.
equation.assumptions: Evaluated at steady-state once Vavg has settled.

sky130_expected.calculation: In Sky130 1.8V standard devices, buffer propagation delay is typically around 0.5 ns to 1.5 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Complementary input pairs provide fast transition times into the inverter stage.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench for the DC reference generation circuit and slicing buffer under 50 MHz input data over 300 ns, measuring channel time constant, input attenuation, peak/valley voltages, reference settling, and output delays.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Figure 18.28 & 18.30: DC Generation Circuit
.lib "/home/designer/shared_pdk/sky130A/libs.tech/ngspice/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* Parameter definitions for parameterized netlist
.param W_xm1=2.0u  L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=2.0u  L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=4.0u  L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=4.0u  L_xm4=0.15u
.param W_xm5=4.0u  L_xm5=0.15u
.param W_xm6=2.0u  L_xm6=0.15u
.param W_xm7=2.0u  L_xm7=0.15u
.param W_xm8=2.0u  L_xm8=0.15u
.param W_xm9=4.0u  L_xm9=0.15u
.param W_xm10=4.0u L_xm10=0.15u
.param W_xm11=2.0u L_xm11=0.15u
.param W_xm12=4.0u L_xm12=0.15u

* Power Supplies
VDD VDD 0 1.8

* Input Data Signal: 50 MHz pulses (20ns period, 10ns width)
Vvin Vin 0 PULSE(0 1.8 10n 0.1n 0.1n 10n 20n)

* Circuit Under Test (Figures 18.28 and 18.30)
X_U1 Max In N001 VDD 0 SUB_1
X_U2 Min In N002 VDD 0 SUB_1
X_U3 In Avg Out VDD 0 SUB_1
xm1 Max N001 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
xm2 Min N002 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
C1 Max 0 1e-12
C2 0 Min 1e-12
C3 Avg 0 1e-12
R1 Max Avg 100000.0
R2 Avg Min 100000.0
R3 Vin In 1000.0
C4 In 0 1e-11
R4 VDD In 1000.0
R5 In 0 1000.0

* Subcircuit Definition from Figure 18.23
.subckt SUB_1 Vinp Vinm Out VDD GND
  xm1 N004 Vinm N005 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
  xm3 N004 N004 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
  xm4 N002 N004 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
  xm2 N002 Vinp N005 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
  xm6 N005 N004 GND 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
  xm5 Out N002 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
  xm7 Out N002 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
  xm8 N003 N003 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
  xm9 N003 Vinm N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm9} l={L_xm9}
  xm10 N002 Vinp N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm10} l={L_xm10}
  xm11 N002 N003 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm11} l={L_xm11}
  xm12 N001 N003 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm12} l={L_xm12}
.ends SUB_1

.control
tran 0.1n 300n

* Measure input node In levels in steady state
meas tran v_in_min min v(in) from=200n to=300n
meas tran v_in_max max v(in) from=200n to=300n
let delta_vin = v_in_max - v_in_min
let attenuation = delta_vin / 1.8
print delta_vin attenuation

* Measure channel effective 10% to 90% rise time to verify tau_eff = tr / 2.2
meas tran t_rise trig v(in) val=0.66 rise=2 targ v(in) val=1.14 rise=2
let tau_channel_eff = t_rise / 2.197
print tau_channel_eff

* Measure DC generator peak, valley, and average voltages
meas tran v_peak_steady find v(Max) at=290n
meas tran v_valley_steady find v(Min) at=290n
meas tran v_avg_steady find v(Avg) at=290n
let calculated_avg = (v_peak_steady + v_valley_steady) / 2
print v_peak_steady v_valley_steady v_avg_steady calculated_avg

* Measure output swing of slicing buffer
meas tran v_out_min min v(Out) from=200n to=300n
meas tran v_out_max max v(Out) from=200n to=300n
print v_out_min v_out_max

* Measure propagation delays
meas tran t_plh trig v(in) val=0.90 rise=10 targ v(Out) val=0.90 rise=10
meas tran t_phl trig v(in) val=0.90 fall=10 targ v(Out) val=0.90 fall=10
let t_pd = (t_plh + t_phl) / 2
print t_plh t_phl t_pd

quit
.endc
.end
